markdownRemark.html:
Freya cannot be tricked into coming forth, as that is of great disrespect to her. An act of ill intent.

The setting can only be made welcoming for Freya to come forth and enter into.

With a set scene, come forth my queen, Sweet goddess of love and beauty, I pray that you be here with me, A sweet union that's meant to be.

Not only the setting, but the individual themself, must be prepared and made ready to be in the presence of divine beauty and grace. This itself is the main work of the invocation. One must be ready for the presence of the divine goddess, and the setting must be made worthy of being graced by her.

Only when yourself and the setting has been made ready and worthy will there be a chance that the goddess can be called forth. The environment is an extension of the individual, via which the individual will be judged whether or not to be worthy of the presence of most high Freya.

Shape the world as well as yourself, Then with her presence you'll be blessed, A rose bed and evening bird song, All that she'd want to be among.

Make yourself and the setting ready, such that Freya would be willing to grace you with her presence. Only then invite her in. Success is wholly dependent on the works of preparation.

The altar is built ready for the goddess that we wish to see.
